I was thinking that there's lots of good suppliers of parts and information around the Internet but it's difficult to sometimes get that one piece of crucial information or a part amongst all the millions of results returned by Google.

Let's share our sources and maybe get the most popular ones linked in the sidebar to help each other out.

I'm in Australia so most of my links will be around here.

Parts and Machinery Suppliers

  • Small Parts and Bearings

    These guys seem to have just about everything you could want in small hardware.

  • Bunnings

    One of the largest hardware store chains in Australia. Fairly reasonable prices locally.

  • Masters

    The other largest chain of hardware stores in Australia.

    Note: If you don't like supporting the Woolworths or Coles behemoths, don't shop at Bunnings or Masters.

  • Jaycar

    Jaycar are like Dick Smiths and Tandy (Radio Shack) used to be years ago. Their hobby and toy sections are getting bigger but they still have a good supply of electronic parts and tools.

  • Hare and Forbes

    This place seems to have every "heavy tool" you could need to work with wood or metal at home or on the job. I have used two of their products on a regular basis on the job (large drill press and a bandsaw) and although they weren't quite Heavy Industry tools they did alright for working with stainless steel and aluminium.

Information

  • G.James Glass and Aluminium

    One of the manufacturers I like because they've got lots of information on their site available to help with figuring out what, where, and how to do your own windows and doors.

    Go to the Professional Section from the front page and it's chock full of info relevant to renovators.

  • Stegbar

    In Stegbar's Info Center there's downloadable PDF's detailing their range of doors and windows, also relevant for home renovators.

  • OneSteel

    In the publications section, there's information on Aluminium, Stainless Steel, and Mild Steel for all manner of construction.

Forums

  • Woodworking Australia Woodwork Forums

    Big forum that also has a section for metal working.

Software

  • SketchUp

    Whether you're designing something big or small, this program is pretty simple to use yet very useful too. I've used SketchUp to design everything from work benches to tool chests to little hobby architectural stuff. Unless I'm mistaken the free version is almost as useful as the pro software - minus the ability to create Dynamic Components, but still able to use them.

  • Kerkythea

    A multi-platform free 3D renderer which works with SketchUp and other 3D CAD programs.

Hey bill.lee. Not the moderator of /v/medicine but I'd just like to say that I agree with what /v/medicine has done, to a certain extent and view it as being justified. Let's examine the typology of /v/medicine users.

  1. Academics & Students: this is the group that immediately comes to mind. You may have researchers, grad students and undergrads in the field who have questions regarding, or wish to have discussions pertaining to their work and studies. Lets imagine what some typical posts & comments would look like. A discussion on the pharmacology of SSRIs on dopaminergic pathways, questions on the effects of some other drug on gonadotropin excretion, a discussion on how new hepatitis treatment drug works and it's long term side effects, if any. This is academic discourse by people interested in the science of medicine. Key word being science and research.

  2. People who are mildly interested in learning about medicine: this is related to the previous group but may not be as interested in medicine as a topic in a hardcore way. They might have questions to ask to someone in medicine, e.g.: "I read that doctors usually are required to do x,y,z in practice, why is this so?", "I'm thinking of going into nursing, what sort of preparations can I make?", "My doctor diagnosed me as having eczema, but ... is it advisble to get a second opinion?", "Is chiropractice a pseudoscience?", etc.

  3. People who are interested in the politics and economics of medicine. This is more of a discussion on the practice of medicine in society, the healthcare system. Tangential topics include, accessibility of healthcare to the poor, the pay of doctors, the scarcity of nurses in America, or some other topic like that unrelated to the science of medicine. We may get submissions like, "Insurance in Ohio not covering [a certain treatment]," "How to reform healthcare in America," "The biotech industry is in a bubble," etc. Notice these are all of a political and economic nature.

  4. People who are interested in the discussion of the medicine industry. Actually, we can split this group into two. The two examples here: investors who are interested in a biotech company and want to ask questions regarding potential FDA approval for a drug in the works, anti-industry discussion such as those of activists who want to attack the wrongdoing of a company. Yes, this includes the conspirary minded people who want to discuss whether Pfizer's board of directors is scheming something behind the scenes.

  5. The last group? Well, this could be enthusiasts of alternative medicine. People who want to discuss TCM, acupuncture, preventative medicine, new age medicine or alternative treatments.

Given this, can they all co-exist on the same subverse? Sure, but it'd be somewhat chaotic. It'd also be off putting to any one group. A student of medicine isn't interested in seeing an activist discussing the evils of Gilead Sciences Inc., an activist isn't interested in hearing about the effects of beta blockers on the nervous system, and investor isn't interested in hearing about either!

Which groups needs medicine the most? Which group is the most popular? Which group should we support? Well, why even think of it that way? This is a constraint of the current system where a single subverse is given a single topic, with everyone else forced to either stay out due to rules, or create their own obscure subverses- How many people will even known /v/uncensoredmedicine exists a year from now? What if an activist goes to /v/medicine, sees a bunch of medical practice jargon and is turned off by that discourse? What if he submits his post and it gets deleted? He might be discouraged from using the site if he doesn't know about /v/uncensoredmedicine. This would similarly apply to someone interested in alternative medicine.

My solution is to have multiple co-existing subverses for a given topic.

So then if one wants a verse fitted towards academic medicine, then they should make one title /v/AcademicMedicine. You don't make a broad topic discussion and then not permit certain aspects of the topic. And chaos is what reddit was built on. If one wants to study medicine with a close mind, and support BigPharma funded schools they are completely welcome them. But people who are more tuned to all perspectives have the greater wisdom to share, and it should be shared openly.
